blocks.en: 1. When the Question Comes
blocks.es_reference: 1. Cuando llega la pregunta

blocks.en: A pastor in a small church in Mexico stands before thirty-five people on a Sunday morning. He has worked two jobs all week and slept four hours the night before. A woman raises her hand. Her son is sick. “Pastor,” she asks, “does the Bible say that if I have enough faith, God will heal him right now?”
blocks.es_reference: Un pastor en una iglesia pequeña de México se para ante treinta y cinco personas un domingo por la mañana. Ha trabajado dos empleos toda la semana y ha dormido cuatro horas la noche anterior. Una mujer levanta la mano. Su hijo está enfermo. —Pastor —pregunta—, ¿dice la Biblia que si tengo suficiente fe, Dios lo sanará ahora mismo?

blocks.en: That question may sound simple. It is not. Behind it stand a thousand sermons the woman has heard on television. Behind it stand the cults that have visited her door. Behind it stand the prosperity teachers who told her that faith is a switch — flip it and God must obey. And in front of that pastor stand thirty-five souls who will believe whatever he says next.
blocks.es_reference: Esa pregunta puede sonar sencilla. No lo es. Detrás de ella están mil sermones que la mujer ha escuchado en televisión. Detrás de ella están las sectas que han tocado a su puerta. Detrás de ella están los maestros de prosperidad que le dijeron que la fe es un interruptor — actívelo y Dios tiene que obedecer. Y delante de ese pastor están treinta y cinco almas que creerán lo que él diga a continuación.

blocks.en: This is why we study hermeneutics. Not to become professors. Not to impress anyone with long Greek words. We study it because a real woman has a real son and she needs a real answer from a real Word of God — and we, the pastors, must be ready to give it.
blocks.es_reference: Por eso estudiamos hermenéutica. No para volvernos profesores. No para impresionar a nadie con palabras griegas largas. La estudiamos porque una mujer real tiene un hijo real y necesita una respuesta real de una Palabra real de Dios — y nosotros, los pastores, debemos estar listos para dársela.

blocks.en: 2. The Word in My Own Heart
blocks.es_reference: 2. La Palabra en mi propio corazón

blocks.en: A boy was reading his Bible when his father caught him. The father snatched the book and threw it into the fire. The boy was still smiling. “Why are you smiling?” the father asked. The boy pointed to his chest and answered, “Because you cannot burn the Bible in here.”
blocks.es_reference: Un niño leía su Biblia cuando su padre lo descubrió. El padre le arrebató el libro y lo arrojó al fuego. El niño seguía sonriendo. —¿Por qué sonríes? —preguntó el padre. El niño señaló su pecho y respondió: —Porque no puedes quemar la Biblia que está aquí adentro.

blocks.en: I was raised in a home like Timothy’s. The Bible was loved and believed. When I was a child I accepted it as the Word of God because that is what my parents taught me. As I grew older my confidence was shaken from time to time — that happens to every honest believer. But I know now that a simple, childlike confidence in the Bible is the goal of every Christian, and especially of every pastor. The Word of God is the well from which we draw water for thirsty people. If the well is poisoned, our people will die.
blocks.es_reference: Yo fui criado en un hogar como el de Timoteo. La Biblia era amada y creída. Cuando era niño la acepté como Palabra de Dios porque eso era lo que mis padres me enseñaban. Al crecer mi confianza fue sacudida de vez en cuando — eso le pasa a todo creyente honesto. Pero ahora sé que una confianza sencilla, como la de un niño, en la Biblia es la meta de todo cristiano, y especialmente de todo pastor. La Palabra de Dios es el pozo del cual sacamos agua para gente sedienta. Si el pozo está envenenado, nuestro pueblo morirá.

blocks.en: 3. Paul’s Charge to Timothy
blocks.es_reference: 3. El encargo de Pablo a Timoteo

blocks.en: In a cold Roman cell, an old apostle wrote to a young pastor. The letter is Second Timothy. The civilization around him was rotting. Paul knew his head was about to roll. And the line he wrote to his son in the faith was this:
blocks.es_reference: En una celda romana fría, un viejo apóstol escribía a un pastor joven. La carta es Segunda de Timoteo. La civilización a su alrededor se estaba pudriendo. Pablo sabía que pronto le cortarían la cabeza. Y la línea que escribió a su hijo en la fe fue ésta:

blocks.en: “Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.” (2 Timothy 2:15, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Procura con diligencia presentarte a Dios aprobado, como obrero que no tiene de qué avergonzarse, que trace bien la palabra de verdad.» (2 Timoteo 2:15, RVG)

blocks.en: Two words sit at the center of that verse: rightly dividing. The Greek word means to cut a straight line — what a carpenter does, what a road-builder does, what a farmer does in plowing a furrow. Paul does not tell Timothy to add to the Word. He does not tell him to subtract from it. He tells him to handle it straight. This is the calling of every pastor. The Word is not ours to remodel. It is ours to deliver.
blocks.es_reference: Dos palabras están en el centro de ese versículo: trazar bien. La palabra griega significa cortar una línea recta — lo que hace un carpintero, lo que hace un constructor de caminos, lo que hace un labrador al arar un surco. Pablo no le dice a Timoteo que añada a la Palabra. No le dice que reste. Le dice que la maneje recta. Éste es el llamado de todo pastor. La Palabra no es nuestra para remodelar. Es nuestra para entregar.

blocks.en: 4. Ezra’s Heart — Study, Do, Teach
blocks.es_reference: 4. El corazón de Esdras: estudiar, hacer, enseñar

blocks.en: Six hundred years before Timothy received his letter, a priest named Ezra came back from Babylon to a ruined Jerusalem. The temple was rebuilt but the people had forgotten the Law. Ezra walked into that mess carrying a scroll. And in chapter seven verse ten the Scripture tells us how he did it:
blocks.es_reference: Seiscientos años antes de que Timoteo recibiera su carta, un sacerdote llamado Esdras regresaba de Babilonia a una Jerusalén en ruinas. El templo había sido reconstruido, pero el pueblo había olvidado la Ley. Esdras entró en ese desorden cargando un rollo. Y en el capítulo siete versículo diez la Escritura nos dice cómo lo hizo:

blocks.en: “Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the Law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel.” (Ezra 7:10, NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: «Porque Esdras había preparado su corazón para inquirir la ley de Jehová, y para cumplirla, y para enseñar en Israel sus estatutos y juicios.» (Esdras 7:10, RVG)

blocks.en: Mark those three things. Study. Do. Teach. Ezra did not prepare his facts, his logic, or his intellect. He prepared his heart. And the order matters. He studied before he taught. He obeyed before he taught. He did not climb into a pulpit to instruct others in commandments he himself had not obeyed.
blocks.es_reference: Marque esas tres cosas. Estudiar. Hacer. Enseñar. Esdras no preparó sus datos, su lógica, ni su intelecto. Preparó su corazón. Y el orden importa. Estudió antes de enseñar. Obedeció antes de enseñar. No subió a un púlpito a instruir a otros en mandamientos que él mismo no había obedecido.

blocks.en: This is the pastor’s threefold posture, and it is the trellis on which our whole course hangs. We may be Bible students. But are we Bible doers? And are we teaching what we ourselves have first studied and obeyed? A pastor who studies and does not do becomes a hypocrite. A pastor who does and does not teach becomes a hoarder. A pastor who teaches and has not first studied becomes a danger. All three — study, do, teach — together.
blocks.es_reference: Ésta es la postura triple del pastor, y es el enrejado sobre el cual cuelga todo nuestro curso. Podemos ser estudiantes de la Biblia. Pero ¿somos hacedores de la Biblia? ¿Y estamos enseñando lo que nosotros mismos primero hemos estudiado y obedecido? Un pastor que estudia y no hace se vuelve un hipócrita. Un pastor que hace y no enseña se vuelve un acaparador. Un pastor que enseña y no ha estudiado primero se vuelve un peligro. Los tres — estudiar, hacer, enseñar — juntos.

blocks.en: 5. What the Scriptures Are
blocks.es_reference: 5. Lo que son las Escrituras

blocks.en: Before we learn how to interpret the Bible, we must know what we are holding. Paul tells Timothy in 2 Timothy 3:15–17 five things about the Scriptures. Each one shapes how a pastor approaches the text.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de aprender cómo interpretar la Biblia, debemos saber qué tenemos en la mano. Pablo le dice a Timoteo en 2 Timoteo 3:15–17 cinco cosas acerca de las Escrituras. Cada una moldea cómo el pastor se acerca al texto.

blocks.en: The Scriptures are teachable. “From childhood you have known the Holy Scriptures.” Timothy learned the Bible at his mother’s knee. The Jews said it was better for a child to forget his own name than to forget the Law of God. Parents and pastors are both teachers. A pastor who cannot make the Bible understandable to a child has not yet understood it himself.
blocks.es_reference: Las Escrituras son enseñables. «Desde la niñez has sabido las Sagradas Escrituras.» Timoteo aprendió la Biblia sobre las rodillas de su madre. Los judíos decían que era mejor para un niño olvidar su propio nombre que olvidar la Ley de Dios. Padres y pastores son ambos maestros. Un pastor que no puede hacer la Biblia comprensible para un niño no la ha comprendido él mismo todavía.

blocks.en: The Scriptures are holy. “Sacred letters,” the Greek says. The word holy means set apart, different. Voltaire said, “One hundred years from now the Bible and Christ will be forgotten.” The very room in which he spoke those words is now used as a Bible storehouse. Henry V of England made Bible-reading a capital crime. His decrees could not shorten its life by one minute or lighten its weight by one ounce. This is not an ordinary book.
blocks.es_reference: Las Escrituras son santas. «Letras sagradas», dice el griego. La palabra santo significa apartado, diferente. Voltaire dijo: «Dentro de cien años la Biblia y Cristo serán olvidados.» La misma habitación donde pronunció esas palabras se usa hoy como almacén de Biblias. Enrique V de Inglaterra hizo de la lectura de la Biblia un crimen capital. Sus decretos no pudieron acortar su vida ni un minuto ni aligerar su peso ni una onza. Este no es un libro ordinario.

blocks.en: The Scriptures lead to salvation. They are “able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Jesus Christ.” Notice — we are not saved by the Bible. The Bible is not a magic charm. Satan knows the Bible and is not saved. We are saved by trusting Christ who is revealed in the Bible. The Word points us to the Person.
blocks.es_reference: Las Escrituras llevan a la salvación. Son «capaces de hacerte sabio para la salvación por la fe que es en Cristo Jesús». Note — no somos salvos por la Biblia. La Biblia no es un amuleto mágico. Satanás conoce la Biblia y no es salvo. Somos salvos al confiar en Cristo, quien es revelado en la Biblia. La Palabra nos señala a la Persona.

blocks.en: The Scriptures are inspired by God. “All Scripture is God-breathed.” In Athens, the Parthenon has not one straight line in its whole structure — the Greeks built it crooked because they knew the human eye sees crookedly. We cannot trust our own eyes. We can rest on the Word of God.
blocks.es_reference: Las Escrituras son inspiradas por Dios. «Toda Escritura es inspirada por Dios.» En Atenas, el Partenón no tiene ni una sola línea recta en toda su estructura — los griegos lo construyeron torcido porque sabían que el ojo humano ve torcido. No podemos confiar en nuestros propios ojos. Podemos descansar en la Palabra de Dios.

blocks.en: The Scriptures are valuable — for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness. William Bieder-Wolf asked, “Did you ever hear a man say, I was a beast as a husband, and then I studied a little geology — and now my brutality is changed to kindness? Did you ever hear that?” No. But the Word of God has transformed millions.
blocks.es_reference: Las Escrituras son valiosas — para enseñar, redargüir, corregir, e instruir en justicia. William Bieder-Wolf preguntó: «¿Ha oído alguna vez a un hombre decir, era una bestia como esposo, y entonces estudié un poco de geología, y ahora mi brutalidad ha cambiado en bondad? ¿Lo ha oído?» No. Pero la Palabra de Dios ha transformado a millones.

blocks.en: 6. How People Respond — The Five C’s
blocks.es_reference: 6. Cómo responde la gente: las cinco C

blocks.en: A second sermon, on 2 Peter 1:21, taught me five reactions people have when the Word of God comes among them. Watch for all five in your own church.
blocks.es_reference: Un segundo sermón, sobre 2 Pedro 1:21, me enseñó cinco reacciones que tiene la gente cuando la Palabra de Dios viene entre ellos. Esté atento a las cinco en su propia iglesia.

blocks.en: Some contend with it. They argue. They divide. Charles Spurgeon said, “Defend the Bible? I would as soon defend a lion.” The Word does not need our protection. Set it loose; it defends itself.
blocks.es_reference: Algunos contienden con ella. Discuten. Dividen. Charles Spurgeon dijo: «¿Defender la Biblia? Sería como defender a un león.» La Palabra no necesita nuestra protección. Suéltela; ella se defiende sola.

blocks.en: Some confuse it. They twist it. The United States alone has more than three hundred fifty sects and cults, most of them claiming to base their teaching on the Bible. Many use the same words, the same verses, the same services — but preach another gospel. The serpent in Eden was the first to do this: “Has God really said?”
blocks.es_reference: Algunos la confunden. La tuercen. Solo Estados Unidos tiene más de trescientas cincuenta sectas, la mayoría afirmando basar su enseñanza en la Biblia. Muchas usan las mismas palabras, los mismos versículos, los mismos servicios — pero predican otro evangelio. La serpiente en el Edén fue la primera en hacer esto: «¿Conque Dios os ha dicho?»

blocks.en: Some condemn it. B. H. Carroll, who later founded Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary, was once a bitter young man who rejected the Bible openly. In 1865 his mother begged him to attend one camp meeting. The preacher asked, “You who stand aloof from Christianity — have you found anything worth having where you are?” Carroll’s heart answered, “Nothing under the whole heaven; absolutely nothing.” That night the bitter scholar was broken.
blocks.es_reference: Algunos la condenan. B. H. Carroll, quien más tarde fundó el Seminario Teológico Bautista Suroccidental, fue una vez un joven amargado que rechazaba la Biblia abiertamente. En 1865 su madre le rogó que asistiera a una reunión campestre. El predicador preguntó: «Ustedes que se mantienen alejados del cristianismo, ¿han encontrado algo digno de tener donde están?» El corazón de Carroll respondió: «Nada bajo todo el cielo; absolutamente nada.» Esa noche el erudito amargado fue quebrantado.

blocks.en: Some conceal it. King Jehoiakim burned Jeremiah’s scroll. God told Jeremiah to write another. In our day Satan no longer burns Bibles. He lets us own them and leave them on shelves.
blocks.es_reference: Algunos la ocultan. El rey Joacim quemó el rollo de Jeremías. Dios le dijo a Jeremías que escribiera otro. En nuestros días Satanás ya no quema Biblias. Nos las deja tener y dejarlas en estantes.

blocks.en: Some confirm it. Billy Graham, in a crisis of doubt, climbed the Sierra Nevada mountains with his Bible. He knelt and prayed, “Father, I cannot understand many things in this book. I cannot come intellectually all the way, but I accept it by faith to be the authoritative, inspired Word of the living God.” From that hour his ministry was unstoppable.
blocks.es_reference: Algunos la confirman. Billy Graham, en una crisis de duda, subió a las montañas de la Sierra Nevada con su Biblia. Se arrodilló y oró: «Padre, no entiendo muchas cosas en este libro. No puedo llegar intelectualmente todo el camino, pero la acepto por fe como la Palabra autoritativa e inspirada del Dios viviente.» Desde esa hora su ministerio fue imparable.

blocks.en: Five reactions — contend, confuse, condemn, conceal, confirm. Your people will show you all five.
blocks.es_reference: Cinco reacciones: contender, confundir, condenar, ocultar, confirmar. Su pueblo le mostrará las cinco.

blocks.en: 7. The Dangers in Our Day
blocks.es_reference: 7. Los peligros de nuestros días

blocks.en: Three dangers press on the small-church pastor today, and a pastor who cannot interpret his Bible will fall into them.
blocks.es_reference: Tres peligros presionan al pastor de iglesia pequeña hoy, y un pastor que no sepa interpretar su Biblia caerá en ellos.

blocks.en: The prosperity twist. I have known pastors who used Jeremiah 29:11 — “I know the thoughts I think toward you, thoughts of peace and not of evil” — at every funeral and every financial crisis. The verse was written to Jews in Babylonian exile facing seventy more years of captivity. When the pastor learned the context, his ministry deepened. His people stopped expecting magic and started trusting God in suffering.
blocks.es_reference: El giro de la prosperidad. He conocido pastores que usaban Jeremías 29:11 — «Yo sé los pensamientos que tengo acerca de vosotros, pensamientos de paz, y no de mal» — en cada funeral y en cada crisis financiera. El versículo fue escrito a judíos en el exilio babilónico que enfrentaban setenta años más de cautiverio. Cuando el pastor aprendió el contexto, su ministerio se profundizó. Su pueblo dejó de esperar magia y comenzó a confiar en Dios en el sufrimiento.

blocks.en: The cult twist. Mormons, Jehovah’s Witnesses, Moonies, and others knock on doors with the same Bible in their hands. They speak the same words but mean different things. Without good interpretation, your people will mistake error for truth — because error speaks fluent Bible.
blocks.es_reference: El giro de las sectas. Mormones, Testigos de Jehová, Moonies, y otros tocan puertas con la misma Biblia en sus manos. Hablan las mismas palabras pero quieren decir cosas diferentes. Sin buena interpretación, su pueblo confundirá el error con la verdad — porque el error habla Biblia con fluidez.

blocks.en: The modernist twist. Other teachers claim the name of Christian but deny the inspiration of the Word, the virgin birth, the resurrection, the miracles. The greatest decline of churches in the last generation has been in those that lost the Bible’s authority. People will not come to hear the ideas of men. They will come to hear a word from God.
blocks.es_reference: El giro modernista. Otros maestros reclaman el nombre de cristiano pero niegan la inspiración de la Palabra, el nacimiento virginal, la resurrección, los milagros. La mayor declinación de iglesias en la última generación ha sido en aquellas que perdieron la autoridad de la Biblia. La gente no vendrá a oír las ideas de los hombres. Vendrá a oír una palabra de Dios.

blocks.en: 8. Guard the Truth — Soldier, Athlete, Farmer
blocks.es_reference: 8. Guarde la verdad: soldado, atleta, labrador

blocks.en: Paul gave Timothy three pictures of the pastor who handles the Word rightly.
blocks.es_reference: Pablo dio a Timoteo tres figuras del pastor que maneja la Palabra rectamente.

blocks.en: Be a soldier — that is dedication. No sideline. One mission. You cannot follow Christ while pursuing five other aims.
blocks.es_reference: Sea un soldado — eso es dedicación. Sin distracciones. Una sola misión. No se puede seguir a Cristo mientras se persiguen otros cinco objetivos.

blocks.en: Be an athlete — that is discipline. No shortcuts, no cutting corners, no breaking the rules. An athlete is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
blocks.es_reference: Sea un atleta — eso es disciplina. Sin atajos, sin recortes, sin romper las reglas. Un atleta no es coronado a menos que compita conforme a las reglas.

blocks.en: Be a farmer — that is diligence. The farmer who expects a harvest in October must work the soil in April. Bible study is field labor. The Word does not yield to the lazy.
blocks.es_reference: Sea un labrador — eso es diligencia. El labrador que espera una cosecha en octubre debe trabajar el suelo en abril. El estudio de la Biblia es labor del campo. La Palabra no da fruto al perezoso.

blocks.en: Dedication, discipline, and diligence. Three pictures, one calling. Combine them with Ezra’s three actions — study, do, teach — and you have the working life of a faithful pastor.
blocks.es_reference: Dedicación, disciplina, y diligencia. Tres figuras, un solo llamado. Combínelas con las tres acciones de Esdras — estudiar, hacer, enseñar — y tiene la vida laboral de un pastor fiel.

blocks.en: 9. The Road Ahead — Seven Principles
blocks.es_reference: 9. El camino por delante: siete principios

blocks.en: In the units to come we will learn seven principles that govern how a pastor reads his Bible faithfully. I introduce them here so you know where we are going.
blocks.es_reference: En las unidades que vienen aprenderemos siete principios que gobiernan cómo un pastor lee fielmente su Biblia. Los presento aquí para que sepa adónde vamos.

blocks.en: First, exegesis before application — draw the meaning out of the text before you carry it into the pulpit. Second, Scripture interprets Scripture — let clear passages explain difficult ones. Third, parables are not allegories — most of Christ’s parables make one principal point, not a dozen hidden ones. Fourth, many miracles are also enacted signs — they can preach as well as demonstrate power and compassion. Fifth, genre determines interpretation — read poetry as poetry, narrative as narrative, prophecy as prophecy. Sixth, literal does not always mean literalistic — Jesus called Himself a door without becoming wood. And seventh, the goal of interpretation is transformation — we are not aiming at information but at changed lives.
blocks.es_reference: Primero, la exégesis antes de la aplicación — saque el significado del texto antes de llevarlo al púlpito. Segundo, la Escritura interpreta la Escritura — deje que los pasajes claros expliquen los difíciles. Tercero, las parábolas no son alegorías — la mayoría de las parábolas de Cristo hacen un punto principal, no una docena de puntos ocultos. Cuarto, muchos milagros también son señales representadas — pueden predicar tanto como demuestran poder y compasión. Quinto, el género determina la interpretación — lea la poesía como poesía, la narrativa como narrativa, la profecía como profecía. Sexto, literal no siempre significa literalista — Jesús se llamó a Sí mismo una puerta sin volverse madera. Y séptimo, la meta de la interpretación es la transformación — no apuntamos a la información sino a vidas cambiadas.

blocks.en: Each principle will get a unit of its own. Each will rest on the Bible itself, not on a textbook.
blocks.es_reference: Cada principio tendrá su propia unidad. Cada uno descansará sobre la Biblia misma, no sobre un libro de texto.

blocks.en: 10. A Closing Charge
blocks.es_reference: 10. Encargo de cierre

blocks.en: The last words Paul ever wrote to Timothy were four: Preach the Word. Be ready in season and out of season. Convince the doubting. Rebuke the sinning. Encourage the fearful. Do it in the presence of God.
blocks.es_reference: Las últimas palabras que Pablo escribió a Timoteo fueron cuatro: Predica la Palabra. Está preparado a tiempo y fuera de tiempo. Convence al que duda. Reprende al que peca. Anima al temeroso. Hazlo en la presencia de Dios.

blocks.en: You are not studying this course to earn a credential. You are studying it so the woman in your church with a sick son will hear a Word from God when she asks her question. That is enough reason to study every page that follows.
blocks.es_reference: Usted no está estudiando este curso para ganar una credencial. Lo está estudiando para que la mujer en su iglesia con un hijo enfermo oiga una Palabra de Dios cuando haga su pregunta. Esa es razón suficiente para estudiar cada página que sigue.

mc.stem: What does Paul mean by "rightly dividing the word of truth" in 2 Timothy 2:15?
options: Adding cultural relevance to the original text
Memorizing as many verses as possible
Handling Scripture straight, without adding or subtracting
Translating it into the language of the people
mc.why: Correct. The Greek word means to cut a straight line — like a carpenter or a road-builder. The pastor delivers the Word straight, not remodeled.

mc.stem: According to Ezra 7:10, what three actions did Ezra set his heart to do?
options: Read, pray, fast
Study, do, teach
Listen, write, preach
Travel, gather, build
mc.why: Correct. Ezra studied, obeyed, and then taught. The order matters: a pastor must study and obey before he climbs into the pulpit.

mc.stem: In the lesson's framework, a pastor who teaches without first studying becomes:
options: A danger
A teacher
A hypocrite
A hoarder
mc.why: Correct. A pastor who teaches without studying is teaching what he does not yet understand — and that endangers the flock.

mc.stem: Why did Paul highlight that Timothy had known the Scriptures "from childhood"?
options: Children's faith is always stronger than an adult's
Scripture is teachable — it can be learned and passed on
Adults do not need the Word as children do
Only children can truly understand the Bible
mc.why: Correct. The first of the five truths from 2 Tim 3:15 is that Scripture is teachable. Timothy learned it at his mother's knee, and the Jews held that a child should sooner forget his own name than the Law of God.

mc.stem: What does the word "holy" mean when applied to the Scriptures?
options: Without any human authorship
Bound in leather and read in services
Set apart, different from other books
Translated only by approved scholars
mc.why: Correct. The word holy means set apart, different. The Bible is different from every other book, including books about the Bible, because God has set it apart.

mc.stem: The lesson uses Voltaire and Henry V of England as examples of:
options: Translators whose Bible work survives today
Enemies of the Bible whose efforts to suppress it failed
Early manuscript copyists
Theological influences on Paul
mc.why: Correct. Voltaire said the Bible would be forgotten in a hundred years — and the room where he said it now stores Bibles. Henry V made Bible-reading a capital crime. Both failed. The Bible stands because it is holy.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, we are saved by:
options: Believing every doctrine of the Bible
Reading the Bible daily
Owning a Bible and reverencing it
Trusting Christ who is revealed in the Bible
mc.why: Correct. The Bible is not a magic charm. Satan knows the Bible and is not saved. The Bible points us to the Person of Christ, and we are saved by trusting Him.

mc.stem: What does "All Scripture is God-breathed" (2 Tim 3:16) teach about the Bible?
options: Its words are inspired by God Himself
It must be read aloud to be effective
It was given through angels
It was written in a single sitting
mc.why: Correct. God-breathed (theopneustos in Greek) means the very words of Scripture originate in God Himself. He used real men with real personalities, but the message is His.

mc.stem: What does the Parthenon illustration in the lesson teach about Scripture?
options: Greek architects were better than Roman ones
The Bible was written in Greek
We cannot trust our own eyes, but we can rest on the Word of God
Athens was the center of biblical learning
mc.why: Correct. The Parthenon was built with no straight lines because the Greeks knew the human eye sees crookedly. We cannot trust our own eyes — but we can rest on the inspired, God-breathed Word of God.

mc.stem: According to 2 Timothy 3:16, what four uses does Paul give for Scripture?
options: Reading, memorizing, quoting, citing
Translating, copying, preaching, teaching
Singing, praying, preaching, fasting
Teaching, rebuking, correcting, training in righteousness
mc.why: Correct. The four uses are teaching (positive instruction), rebuking (finding our faults), correcting (checking beliefs against the Bible), and training in righteousness (showing what is right and wrong).

mc.stem: What did Charles Spurgeon mean when he said, "Defend the Bible? I would as soon defend a lion"?
options: The Bible is a dangerous book and should be approached with fear
The Bible defends itself when proclaimed; it needs no human protection
Bible defenders must be brave like lion-tamers
The Bible has roared throughout history against its enemies
mc.why: Correct. Just as a lion needs no defender — you simply turn it loose — the Word of God defends itself when proclaimed. Our task is not to argue people into the Bible, but to set it loose among them.

mc.stem: The lesson lists five reactions people have to the Word of God. They are:
options: Read, study, memorize, quote, apply
Hear, believe, reject, doubt, accept
Contend, confuse, condemn, conceal, confirm
Translate, preach, teach, copy, distribute
mc.why: Correct. The five C's, from 2 Peter 1:21: people contend with the Word, confuse it, condemn it, conceal it, or confirm it. A pastor will meet all five reactions in his congregation.

mc.stem: B.H. Carroll's story (the camp meeting of 1865) illustrates which response to the Word?
options: A bitter scholar who once condemned the Bible coming to faith
The early Methodist mission to the American South
The founding of the Southern Baptist Convention
A traveling evangelist's preaching style
mc.why: Correct. Carroll, who later founded Southwestern Baptist Theological Seminary, had been a bitter rejector of the Bible — until the question "Have you found anything worth having where you are?" broke him.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what is Satan's most effective modern strategy against the Bible?
options: Having it burned in public squares
Making laws against owning it
Translating it badly
Letting people own it but never read it
mc.why: Correct. King Jehoiakim burned Jeremiah's scroll; Henry V outlawed Bible-reading. Both failed. Today Satan does not burn Bibles — he lets people own them and leave them on shelves.

mc.stem: Billy Graham's Sierra Nevada crisis ended with him doing what?
options: Accepting the Bible's authority by faith despite remaining intellectual questions
Renouncing his preaching ministry permanently
Writing a new commentary on Romans
Founding a Bible college in California
mc.why: Correct. Graham knelt in the mountains and said, "I cannot come intellectually all the way, but I accept it by faith to be the authoritative, inspired Word of the living God." From that hour his ministry was unstoppable.

mc.stem: The prosperity-teaching misuse of Jeremiah 29:11 is dangerous because:
options: The verse was actually written by Isaiah, not Jeremiah
It was originally addressed to exiles facing more captivity, not to modern wealth-seekers
The verse appears in a footnote, not the main text
The Hebrew word for "welfare" actually means "judgment"
mc.why: Correct. Jeremiah wrote to Jews facing seventy more years of Babylonian captivity. The promise was for endurance through long suffering, not instant prosperity. Context corrects the abuse.

mc.stem: The three pictures Paul gives Timothy of the faithful pastor are:
options: Shepherd, fisherman, builder
Father, teacher, servant
Soldier, athlete, farmer
Priest, prophet, king
mc.why: Correct. Soldier (dedication), athlete (discipline), farmer (diligence). Combined with Ezra's three actions — study, do, teach — they form the working life of the faithful pastor.

mc.stem: The principle "exegesis before application" means:
options: Draw the meaning out of the text before carrying it into the pulpit
Apply the text first, then study its meaning
Apply only verses that have been preached on before
Application is more important than meaning
mc.why: Correct. Exegesis means "drawing out" — drawing the meaning out of the text. We must first know what the text MEANS before we tell our people what it MEANS FOR THEM.

mc.stem: According to the principle "Scripture interprets Scripture," what should govern the meaning of a difficult passage?
options: The pastor's personal experience
The most popular commentary of the day
The cultural mood of the moment
The clear teaching of other Scripture passages
mc.why: Correct. The Bible is its own best commentary. Clear passages illuminate difficult ones. Major doctrines must rest on repeated, clear teaching — never on one isolated obscure verse.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, the ultimate goal of the seven principles of interpretation is:
options: Producing intellectual scholars
Winning theological debates
Memorizing the Bible
Transforming lives
mc.why: Correct. The seventh principle is the heartbeat of the whole course: the goal of interpretation is transformation. We are not aiming at information but at changed lives.

sa.prompt: According to Ezra 7:10, what three actions did Ezra set his heart to do, and why does the order matter for the pastor?
sa.model: Ezra prepared his heart, then set himself to study the Law, to do it, and to teach it. The order is fixed: a pastor must study the Word, then obey and practice it in his own life, before he is fit to teach it to others.

sa.prompt: Explain what Paul means by "rightly dividing the word of truth" in 2 Timothy 2:15, and why this command is foundational for pastoral ministry.
sa.model: Paul tells Timothy to handle the word of truth straight, like a carpenter cutting a straight line. The pastor does not add to it or subtract from it; he divides it accurately and delivers it as it is.

sa.prompt: In 2 Timothy 3:15-17 Paul names five things about the Scriptures. List them and briefly explain each.
sa.model: Paul names that the holy Scriptures are able to make us wise unto salvation, that they are God-breathed and inspired, that they are profitable for teaching and correction, and that they thoroughly equip the man of God for every good work.

sa.prompt: The lesson lists five reactions people have to the Word of God (the Five C's). Name them and briefly describe each.
sa.model: People show five reactions to the Word. Some contend with it and argue; some are confused by it; some condemn and reject it; some conceal it and leave it on the shelf; and some confirm it, accepting it by faith. The pastor will see all five in his people.

sa.prompt: Explain what "All Scripture is God-breathed" (2 Tim 3:16) means, and why this doctrine matters for how a pastor handles the Bible.
sa.model: 'God-breathed' means the very words of Scripture came out of the mouth of God Himself. Their origin is divine, so they carry God's own authority. That is why the pastor handles the Bible as the trustworthy and inspired Word of God, not the opinions of men.

sa.prompt: Describe the prosperity-teaching misuse of Jeremiah 29:11 and explain how proper context corrects it.
sa.model: The prosperity teacher uses Jeremiah 29:11 to promise health and wealth, but the verse was written to Jews in Babylonian exile facing seventy more years of captivity. Read in context, it does not promise an easy life; it promises that God is faithful through suffering. The context corrects the misuse.

sa.prompt: Paul gives Timothy three pictures of the faithful pastor: soldier, athlete, and farmer. Explain what each one teaches the pastor.
sa.model: Paul gives Timothy three pictures. The soldier teaches dedication — one mission, no sideline. The athlete teaches discipline — no shortcuts, competing by the rules. The farmer teaches diligence — patient labor that waits for the harvest and the reward.

sa.prompt: Charles Spurgeon said, "Defend the Bible? I would as soon defend a lion." Explain what this means for how a pastor handles the Word.
sa.model: Spurgeon said he would as soon defend a lion as defend the Bible. The point is that the Word does not need our protection; like a lion, you simply turn it loose and it defends itself. So the pastor's task is not to guard the truth but to proclaim and preach it boldly.

sa.prompt: List at least five of the seven principles of interpretation introduced in this unit, and briefly explain why each matters for the pastor.
sa.model: The seven principles are: exegesis before application — draw the meaning out before carrying it to the pulpit; Scripture interprets Scripture; parables are not allegories but make one principal point; many miracles are also enacted signs that can preach; genre determines interpretation; literal is not literalistic; and the goal of interpretation is transformation, not mere information.

sa.prompt: Why is hermeneutics — the art of interpreting the Bible — a pastoral concern, not merely an academic one? Use the lesson's opening illustration in your answer.
sa.model: Hermeneutics is pastoral because a real woman with a sick son stands before the pastor asking whether faith will heal him, and thirty-five souls will believe whatever he says next. He cannot give an academic lecture; he must give a real answer from the Word of God. Interpreting the Bible rightly is how the pastor protects and feeds his flock.
